sections.title: Habit and alpine habitat
sections.text: Carex curvula is a small, tuft-forming sedge of subalpine and alpine grasslands in Europe, often on poor soils and wind-exposed ridges with little winter snow. Its tufts are about 5–30 cm tall; the very narrow leaves are 1–2 mm wide and the compact inflorescence about 1–1.5 cm long.

sections.title: Spikes and plate
sections.text: The plate shows the tuft of curved leaves, small brownish spikes and a close-up of a perigynium enclosing the fruit, all consistent with a sedge. No food use or particular toxicity has been established well enough to include.
